title: 📅 Build Your Band 9 Study Plan

sections.heading: How long do you need?
sections.body:
Complete beginner (Band 4–5) → Band 7: 3–6 months
Intermediate (Band 5–6) → Band 7: 2–3 months
Intermediate (Band 6) → Band 8: 3–4 months
Advanced (Band 7) → Band 8–9: 1–3 months

These are averages for 1–2 hours of daily study. Results vary significantly with consistency.

sections.heading: The 4-week foundation plan
sections.body:
Week 1: Test format mastery + core vocabulary
Week 2: Reading strategies + grammar foundations
Week 3: Writing Task 1 & 2 structure practice
Week 4: Listening skills + Speaking fluency
Then: Mock tests every weekend + focus on weakest skill

highlight: Consistency beats intensity. 45 minutes every day beats 6 hours on Saturday. Your brain consolidates learning during sleep — daily practice is essential.

question: Which study habit is MOST effective for IELTS preparation?
options: Studying for 8 hours on one day a week
explanation:
Spaced repetition and consistent daily exposure are the most evidence-backed learning strategies.

Benefits of daily study:
• Vocabulary sticks better with repeated exposure over time
• Fluency develops gradually through consistent speaking practice
• Sleep consolidation helps grammar become automatic

8 hours once a week exhausts the brain and retains less.

instruction: Match each weak skill to the best daily practice habit:

pairs.meaning: Watch/listen to BBC, TED Talks, podcasts daily
Read one academic article + practise T/F/NG
Write one paragraph or full essay daily, timed

explanation: The single best predictor of IELTS improvement is the hours of authentic input (listening, reading real academic English) combined with deliberate output practice (writing and speaking daily).

question: You have 8 weeks until your IELTS exam and Writing is your weakest skill (Band 5.5). What should you prioritise?
options: Focus 60% of time on Writing, 40% on others
Only practise Writing and ignore other skills
Take full mock tests every day
correct: Focus 60% of time on Writing, 40% on others
explanation:
With a specific weakness, weight your time toward it without abandoning others:

• Writing: 3–4 sessions/week
• Listening: 1–2 sessions/week (easier to maintain)
• Reading: 1–2 sessions/week
• Speaking: Daily 10-minute recording practice

Ignoring other skills risks them declining. Taking full mock tests daily doesn't provide targeted skill-building.
